name: Read the Label Like a Pro
why_it_works: Shoppers feel tricked by labels and tags, so teaching them where to look hands them power. Once they know what a good label says, they hold every competitor to that standard, and the brand that taught them passes its own test.

hook.pattern: Show a real-looking label with three zones circled and promise the viewer will never shop the same way again.
examples: Before you buy {{product_type}}, check these 3 spots.
The front of the {{product_type}} is marketing. Flip it.
3 spots on any {{product_type}} that don't lie.

variables.name: zone_1_tip
variables.example: 14K or 585 means solid gold. 'GP' or 'GF' means plated or filled.

variables.name: zone_2_tip
variables.example: 'Gold tone' means no gold at all. Look for the karat and the word 'solid'.

variables.name: zone_3_tip
variables.example: Price per gram lets you compare two chains that look identical.

variables.name: red_flag
variables.description: The one phrase that should make shoppers walk away

variables.name: offer
variables.example: Shop our solid gold edit, with karat and grams on every tag

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine print for the client's niche, from the matching pack in compliance/packs.json
variables.example: Results vary. These statements have not been evaluated by the FDA.

cta: Save this for your next purchase. {{offer}}.

slides.headline: Stop reading the front
slides.body: 3 spots on any {{product_type}} that tell the truth.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 close-up photo of the {{product_type}} with its tag or label, three spots circled in bright marker, soft daylight on a neutral linen surface

slides.headline: Spot 1: {{label_zone_1}}
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 macro photo of {{label_zone_1}} on the {{product_type}}, crisp focus, soft studio light, a single circle highlight

slides.headline: Spot 2: {{label_zone_2}}
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 macro photo of {{label_zone_2}} on the {{product_type}} label, crisp focus, soft studio light, a single underline highlight

slides.headline: Spot 3: {{label_zone_3}}
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 macro photo of {{label_zone_3}} on the {{product_type}}, crisp focus, soft studio light, a single arrow highlight

slides.headline: Red flag: walk away
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 photo of an unbranded generic {{product_type}} tag with the vague wording circled in red, cool flat light

slides.headline: Now check ours
slides.body: Every spot is answered on our own label. See for yourself.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 hero photo of the {{brand}} {{product_type}} with its label facing camera, all three spots circled in green, warm premium light

slides.headline: Shop with your eyes open
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 clean {{brand}} logo card with the offer in large type and a save bookmark icon

craft.technique: Teach the test, then pass it
craft.notes: Spend five slides teaching a neutral, brand-free inspection method, and only then show your own label passing it. The order matters: if the brand appears first, the lesson reads as an ad. Use the same circle, underline and arrow graphics throughout so the zones feel like a system.

do_not: Show or name a real competitor's label; use an unbranded generic for the red flag
Teach a check your own product fails
Claim a label term means more than it legally does
compliance: Supplements: no disease claims (treat, cure, prevent); any structure/function claim on screen needs the FDA disclaimer 'These statements have not been evaluated by the Food and Drug Administration'
Supplements: never advise skipping medication or doctor guidance; add 'Ask your doctor before starting supplements'
Skincare: cosmetic claims only; do not call an ingredient a treatment for a medical condition
Jewelry: karat and metal claims must match the item exactly (FTC jewelry guides)
